Real Life Experience in Manu National Park
Overview
Robles Treehouse Lodge – Eco Lodge Near Manu National Park
Experience the beauty of the Manu Biosphere Reserve at Robles Treehouse Lodge, located on the edge of Manu National Park. Surrounded by pristine rainforest and the Palotoa River, our eco-lodge is the perfect base for exploring one of the world's most biodiverse destinations.
Comfortable Jungle Stay
Our lodge features 10 private bungalows with hot showers, private bathrooms, solar power, Wi-Fi, and comfortable beds. Relax in the dining area, enjoy panoramic river views, and watch colorful birds from our lush tropical gardens.
Explore the Amazon
Enjoy guided jungle walks, kayaking, tubing, caiman spotting, boat excursions, parrot and macaw clay lick visits, and breathtaking views from our 30-meter observation tower with expert local guides.
Easy Access
Located around 250 km from Cusco, Robles Treehouse Lodge is reached by road and boat, offering a peaceful escape deep in the Peruvian Amazon.

A Unique Jungle Lodge on the Palotoa River
Our lodge is situated within the Manu Biosphere reserve and on the limits of the famous Manu National Park , which is one of the most biodiverse areas on the planet. The Robles Treehouse Lodge was one of the first lodges to be built within the River Palotoa river basin and today is still considered to be the most important.
The lodge has 10 private bungalows, each equipped for 2 people. All have a hot shower, a toilet area, solar energy and access to Wi-Fi. On the rest of the large grounds there is a big and comfortable dining area with hammocks and deck chairs in addition to a panoramic view of the Palotoa river. Also, on a point which juts out into the river there are several lounge chairs. There is a large green area full of palm and fruit trees as well as many other plants which attract a variety of birds to the area throughout the day.
We have single beds, queen size beds and beds for children so that you can sleep comfortably at night – as if you were in the comfort of your home.
You can use the lodgings as a base for a variety of activities such as, tubing and kayaking on the river, night and daytime walks into the forest, watching caimans on the Huito Cocha lake, nocturnal boat trips along the river, observing a clay lick used by parrots and macaws and climbing up a 30m observation tower for good views of the wildlife and surrounding woodlands.
You will be surrounded by nature and vast landscapes in a way that you may not have experienced before. To help you enjoy this experience we work with local guides who have intimate knowledge of the forest. Take your time in order to enjoy this amazing experience in the heart of the Amazon jungle.

What is Robles Treehouse Lodge?
Robles Treehouse Lodge is a unique rainforest accommodation in the Manu region of Peru, offering guests the opportunity to stay in elevated treehouse-style bungalows surrounded by pristine Amazon nature.
Q2.
Why should I choose a Tree House Lodge in Peru?
A Tree House Lodge Peru experience allows travelers to enjoy panoramic rainforest views, close wildlife encounters, and a peaceful stay above the jungle floor while exploring the Amazon.
Q3.
What can I expect from a Treehouse Lodge in Peru?
A Treehouse Lodge in Peru typically includes private accommodations, guided jungle walks, birdwatching, river excursions, and opportunities to observe the diverse wildlife of the Manu rainforest.

Robles Family Company
Local Jungle Experts Dedicated to Manu National Park
We are a local family business which specializes in Tours to the virgin forests of Manu National Park. Manu Rainforest Peru is one of the few tour operator companies that has the depth of knowledge and broad logistical capabilities to guarantee successful tours to all parts of Manu National Park.
Our small group style of travel means you'll receive personalized attention and will travel, eat and sleep the local way. You'll will have the opportunity to experience how life really is in the jungle and in other rural settings. You'll have the chance to learn from the unsurpassed knowledge of local guides and leaders, taking you beyond the guidebooks and into the exciting world you're looking to discover. Small groups, big adventures!!!
Top guides. We have both the skill and the patience to help you make the most of your experience. We are a friendly team, and all our guides are able to adaptable to the pace and interests of our clients. We speak both English and Spanish. Manu Rainforest Peru is one of the few operators who really understands and provides a good value service for jungle lovers and serious birders alike.
Careful planning and logistics. Our Manu rainforest tours itineraries are carefully planned to ensure that you can maximize the time spent looking for and viewing the wildlife and birds which are of particular interest to you. We aim to minimize wasted time and unnecessary cost and to avoid uncomfortable situations. We want you to enjoy yourselves and to go home with golden memories of your time with us.
Quality tours at reasonable prices. We aim to provide world-class birding and general jungle tours at highly competitive prices. We believe that we offer the best value for money for adventurers and birders visiting Manu.
We talk to our clients in a clear and honest way. We are realistic about the chances of finding certain birds or mammals, and make sure that our clients are aware of them too.

Robles Family Company
From the Jungles of Manu to a Family-Run Tour Operator
My mother, TERESA CONDORI, migrated to the jungle with her parents when she was 9 years old from the Cusco region. Her parents were farmers. Her father was blind so her mother was in charge both at home and working hard every day to survive in the jungle of Manu. My father, SABINO ROBLES, went to the jungle when he was 17 with the Peruvian army. He was so impressed with the natural wonder he found there that he decided to stay. He also worked as a park ranger for Manu National Park in the first years of the park's founding, from 1973. Then he met and married Teresa, my mother. From this marriage they had 6 sons and 3 daughters, ourselves. My mother and my father were excellent farmers. They cultivated, rice, cassava, banana, papaya, beans, sweet potatoes, and many other fruits, etc. Although they were successful at growing so many products, there was no market, so the products had no monetary value. Remote Manu was a region without access, and away from the big cities.
By 2000 agriculture had become more important as a source of income. Cusco became a key market for bananas and, therefore, the local people in Manu dedicated more resources to growing this crop. It became a very important source of income for families. In 2003 my father died from a kidney problem. At the time, my brothers (including the eldest, Saul) and I were still very young. We had to take on the responsibilities of my family. We also became dedicated to growing bananas, our only source of income and work. Five years after high school we had saved some money and I came to Cusco to study for the first time. Despite having to overcome many difficulties I began to study to become an official tour guide.
In 2006 we were ready for tourism. We started traveling with really small groups of just one or two passengers at a time. We had loads of will and enthusiasm. We created a genuine united family business. Back then we only slept in tents. After a few years of working, we decided to build our own lodgings.
Today our family business is very stable. We provide work to many local people in addition to my family. We continue to be very committed. Each of us work together as a team. We don't pretend to be the best! But we want to be! We work hard, and we're getting there!
Today we have our own river boats and our own ground transport. We have our own lodgings, which we have constructed ourselves. And most importantly we have a team of permanent guides, and personnel in each area (my family!).

Frequently Asked Questions
WHAT IS ALTITUDE SICKNESS IN CUSCO?
Arriving in Cusco, located more than 10,800 feet above sea level, from a city where the altitude is quite near sea level can be an uncomfortable experience if you are affected by altitude sickness. Only a person who has experienced it knows how hard it
can knock you out. If you come from a lower town of 6,000 feet, you will need to acclimatize to eliminate the risk of developing altitude sickness during a tour of the Salkantay or other treks like Rainbow Mountain.
Be aware walking the Salkantay and visiting Machu Picchu are high altitude hikes. Don't let altitude sickness ruin one of the best experiences of your life.
In general, symptoms of altitude sickness can be felt already at about 7,000 feet. The chances of getting altitude sickness increases with height. Some of the most common symptoms of altitude sickness are strong headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach cramps
and nose bleeds. For others it can be even more severe. These symptoms are caused by conditions of low atmospheric pressure that occur at high elevations. Before attempting the trek it is recommended that you spend some time at lower
elevations, slowly increasing them, so your body can adjust.
Studies have shown that not everyone gets altitude sickness. Unfortunately, there is no way to know if a person is going to get it. Being in good physical shape does not reduce the risk. Only, once you reach a high altitude, will you know if your body
is affected by the altitude.
If you decide to take the over the counter medicine, you should begin taking it a couple of days before starting the tour. However, it is important to know that this drug does not guarantee that you will not be affected by altitude sickness.
Native Peruvians use a natural source to reduce the effects of altitude sickness, as well as fatigue. This natural source is the coca leaf and needs to be constantly chewed or prepared in tea.
The conventional and most effective method to eliminate the risk of developing altitude sickness is the gradual process of acclimatization to height. Staying in Cusco, Ollantaytambo or any other high altitude city for at least three days prior to the
date of departure for the Salkantay or Rainbow Mountain (or any high altitude hike) will help to eliminate the risk of developing altitude sickness during the trek.
In addition to the methods mentioned above, avoid high energy activities the first two days; you should drink plenty of fluids, avoid caffeine and alcohol, and keep a healthy diet: avoid overeating or eating fatty foods.
IS FOOD INCLUDED IN THE TRIPS?
In general we provide full meals and snacks during the trip starting with lunch on the first day to breakfast on the last day (the last lunch in Aguas Calientes is not included). In the case of travel to the Manu National Park, meals are included until
the last lunch. Our experienced chefs make incredible meals in the midst of the forest or the mountains. They also prepare dishes for people with different lifestyles or food restrictions, so please let us know your preferences and
we will make sure to meet your dietary needs. Bring along your own high energy snacks.
WHAT ARE THE BEST MONTHS TO VISIT PERU?
The best months to do hikes like the Inca Trail, Choquequiraw, Salkantay, Ausangate, and Lares, are from May to September, when conditions are very dry and mostly sunny. However the months of June, July and August can also be very cold at night so bring
good warm clothing (layers) and a 4-season sleeping bag (or you can rent one from us). The terrain of Peru varies from low lying hot jungle to snow capped Andes; Seasons also play a role in conditions.
In the Andes, there are two main seasons - wet and dry. The rainy season runs from November to April and is usually warmer/humid. The dry season extends from May to October and has hot days but cold nights.
There are two distinct seasons in the jungle – damp/rainy or - warm/damp. The rainy season begins in November and stays wet until April. The dry season extends from May to October and has hot days, but in the early hours of the day it’s damp/cold.
The only sure thing that can be said about weather in Peru is that it is difficult to predict with accuracy. You can have a clear hot day and suddenly find yourself in the middle of a hail storm for example. Season and dry wet station - is one of the
beauties of Peru.
HOW OLD DO YOU HAVE TO BE TO TRAVEL WITH MANU RAINFOREST PERU?
The minimum age to travel with Manu Rainforest Peru is seven. Passengers must be at least 18 years of age to travel without their parents or guardians. The only exception is that children under age 18 must to travel with their parents or guardians.
WHAT IF I HAVE SPECIAL DIETARY NEEDS?
If you have special dietary requests, we strongly encourage you to inform Manu Rainforest Peru at the time of booking, or at least by 30 days prior to take the tour. Every effort will be made to cater to special dietary needs, and to accommodate special
requests, subject to a given product’s availability in Peru.
